analysis: The PR changes only documentation. In docs/developer/test.md the changed lines (base 1432-1434, 2057-2061) cover the "Last updated" date, CI job routing prose (all Mac jobs are now routed, including the GPU shards), and the job-shape test description (a `required` lane keeps its fallback while sizes are off, and release workflows stay on literal Blacksmith runners). I examined the two supplied head-text excerpts (lines 2731-3418) of that file; they sit outside the changed ranges and are unchanged test-description context. In docs/operations/provider-release.md the patch bumps the date and adds one statement: a pull-request run on a Darkbloom Sandbox that the plane gave no Darkbloom cache skips the cache steps of .github/actions/provider-release-build, while release workflows never skip them. That keeps the release signing and publication path on Blacksmith runners with cache steps intact. The text says PR caches stay PR-scoped and do not seed master, so the cache-poisoning boundary is not weakened. No runtime code, wire protocol, keys, attestation, prefix-cache storage (T-041), authorization or release-registration behavior changed, and the diff does not alter threat-model assumptions for TB-002, TB-003, TB-007 or TB-011. Open integration questions: the actual workflow files, runner-routing scripts (scripts/ci-*) and the .github/actions skip logic are not in this batch, so I cannot confirm that the documented guarantees (release workflows never skip cache steps; they remain on literal Blacksmith runners) match the implementation. This is a documentation-accuracy question, not an observed regression.
